items.html:
The documentation foundation is substantially complete. Keep the round-4 Material site and generated reference, then integrate the release branch’s versioning, installation and publishing instructions. The remaining work is reconciliation and release-specific accuracy, not a documentation rewrite.

Refs below: I = 1f8b6077 (condensed into 8251007) (improvements), R = bf088769 (release-readiness), A = origin/claude/framework-adapter-fixes.

Required work Evidence and consequence
Keep Material; remove the abandoned custom theme. Binding owner decision in R:HANDOFF.md:35-37, explicit reconciliation instructions at 102-106. Preserve improvements’ pages, navigation, examples, _catalog and generate_docs.py; discard release docs-theme/, custom scripts/mkdocs_hooks.py, check_docs_*.cjs, and old landing page. Reimplement only necessary versioned publishing behavior against Material.
Choose one release procedure. I:docs/development/releasing.md:15-25 says update changelog/citation and tag after local checks. R:RELEASING.md:67-96 says dispatch → tested candidate/TestPyPI → create exact candidate tag → production approval. Retain release workflow sequencing and round-4 changelog/citation preparation. Remove the duplicate contradictory instructions, ideally keeping one authoritative release page with a short root link.
Port documentation deployment correctly. I:docs/development/documentation.md:138-144 and I:docs/development/releasing.md:33-43 describe unversioned Pages behind DOCS_DEPLOY. Owner-approved target is dev, X.Y.Z, latest with mike (R:HANDOFF.md:35-37). Update these pages and CI/development descriptions; add Material’s mike version selector. Preserve rustdoc within each version.
Fix deep links for versioned docs. Current unversioned URLs occur in I:README.md:31-113, Cargo.toml:16, docs/reference/rust.md:8, python/treams_rs/init.py:21, advect.py:35, jax.py:27,136, torch.py:25,124, and generated reference pages. A root redirect to latest does not establish these unversioned deep paths. Update repository/package links to /latest/...; use version-local links inside published pages where appropriate; regenerate generated pages.
Merge the correct source-reference handling. I:docs/_hooks/site.py:51 takes repository link revision from GITHUB_SHA. R:.github/workflows/docs.yml:32,39 supplies TREAMS_RS_DOCS_SOURCE_REF and checks out source_revision, which can differ from the triggering SHA when correcting released docs. Retaining the old hook unchanged links docs to the wrong source revision.
Preserve useful machine-readable docs behavior deliberately. Improvements’ hook only strips fence modes and rewrites links; its llms.txt is a repository index (I:scripts/generate_docs.py:119-144). Release hook publishes version-local llms.txt and Markdown sources (R:scripts/mkdocs_hooks.py:207-229,245-249,301-310). Keep that useful behavior if intended, adapting it to the new generator/header instead of retaining both hooks. The old release header matcher will not match improvements’ header.
Rewrite installation for the actual first release. I:README.md:36-40, docs/getting-started/install.md:9-23,38 still require GitHub/Rust and say “not on PyPI yet.” Make wheels/pip install treams-rs the normal path, list exact wheel targets and optional-extra limits, and retain source-build instructions separately. Do not publish “wheels are built” as verified until hosted builds pass; release handoff explicitly says those platforms were not verified (R:HANDOFF.md:60-64).
Align all support claims with the approved Python matrix. Approved target is CPython 3.12–3.15, with reduced newer-Python oracle coverage accepted (R:HANDOFF.md:32-33). Stale 3.12/3.13-only claims remain at I:README.md:6, install.md:9-15, validation/capabilities.md:79, validation/numerical-limits.md:346-347, development/index.md:9,45-61, validation/index.md:44,86, and CONTRIBUTING.md:22. Match metadata, CI and prose; distinguish core support from optional package availability.
Update contributor setup and verification instructions. I:docs/development/index.md:9-25 pins uv 0.12.3, installs torch through the extra and describes only four hooks. Release uses uv 0.12.22, CPU-wheel torch setup and more hooks (R:docs/development.md). Keep improvements’ directory/test ownership and just ci structure, incorporating actual reconciled commands rather than copying references to deleted flat tests/generators.
Keep the current tested examples, not release’s older API examples. R:README.md:54 calls plane_wave(..., polarization="positive_helicity"). In I:python/treams_rs/_waves.py:527-544, pol is the state and polarization is "helicity"/"parity". Improvements’ quickstart correctly uses pol (I:docs/getting-started/quickstart.md:20,30-32). Update release smoke scripts similarly, then regenerate and execute all documentation examples on the final API.
Separate the current oracle version from historical comparison claims. Release upgrades dev treams to 0.4.7 (R:pyproject.toml:90-94), while improvements consistently describes 0.4.5 in conventions, differences, gallery, contributor guidance and performance evidence. Historical 0.4.5 measurements must remain labeled 0.4.5. Recheck active comparisons/examples under the selected oracle and explain current test oracle versus compatibility/benchmark baseline. Avoid blanket replacement.
Complete attribution for the final implementation. Improvements credits XSF and packages LICENSE.xsf (I:THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md:29-33, CONTRIBUTING.md:76-77, pyproject.toml:11, crates/treams-core/src/special/ferrers.rs:2). Release’s approved clean-room replacement removes that dependency, adds bundled Rust license texts (R:HANDOFF.md:29-31,52-54). Remove XSF claims only after the replacement is actually integrated and verified. Preserve improvements’ treams example attribution (I:THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md:7-8), retain upstream treams notices, regenerate license bundles, remove release’s stale [earlier project] mention (R:THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md:11-12) and fix its old legendre.rs source link (37-39).
Refresh Legendre accuracy explanations with the replacement. I:docs/coming-from-treams/differences.md:92 describes specific old recurrence/series choices and old error bounds. I:docs/validation/index.md:90 reports the historical 2.17e-13 result. Release has a different implementation and requalification. Preserve the old record, add the new one, and update implementation claims and current validation results. Release explicitly instructs restoring the archived result and adding a new file (R:HANDOFF.md:107-109).
Prepare actual 0.1.0 release metadata. I:CITATION.cff lacks treams-rs version/date; I:SECURITY.md:5 says no release exists; I:CHANGELOG.md:5,12 remains pre-release. Add release date/version, supported security version, and final release notes. Preserve citation author [name] and package author “treams-rs contributors,” as the latest owner decision states (origin/r4-tooling:plan/decisions.md:173); release’s metadata instead uses [name] (R:pyproject.toml:27). Git author rewriting is a separate matter.
Condense the changelog, preserving the useful name map. Improvements’ 741-line changelog accumulates intermediate, superseded states: 34-38 says numerical namespaces expose *_with_context, while 99 onward moves those into diff; 55-56 describes contract, while 95-97 renames it. Publish a coherent first-release description and concise pre-release migration/name mapping, rather than presenting every intermediate refactor as final behavior.
Preserve honest benchmark provenance through the squash. I:docs/performance/evidence.md:11-29 refers to original pre-release commits and includes measurements with missing dates/commits; 35-44,64,80 includes explicitly unarchived timings. I:docs/performance/index.md:105-108 already correctly says later revisions were not rerun. Keep original measured hashes as historical identities, never silently replace them with squash hashes that did not produce those results. Preserve recoverable source snapshots for evidence you continue presenting, or label the historical reproducibility limitation. Publish release-head measurements separately; remove or retain unarchived timing anecdotes explicitly as historical rather than elevating them into release evidence.

Additional findings:

  • No remaining “private project/repository/wheel,” personal path, Claude-session, [another GitHub account], or [earlier project] reference was found in the improvements branch’s public README, contributor guide, docs, citation, package metadata, notices or llms.txt by scoped text search. This does not cover full history or benchmark archives.
  • The framework guide already clearly documents CPU execution, first-order gradients, static inputs, framework dtype differences, residual lifetime and unsupported transforms (I:docs/differentiation/frameworks.md:62-78,123-139,273-285). Preserve this specificity; no generic rewrite is needed.
  • Do not resurrect wording/jargon tests: the owner explicitly removed all repository wording enforcement (origin/r4-tooling:plan/decisions.md:172).
  • The SciPy defect report is separate follow-up work, not a prerequisite for publishing this library (R:HANDOFF.md:136-141).
  • Remove temporary branch handoffs after their useful decisions and open items are integrated (R:HANDOFF.md:3, A:HANDOFF.md:6); cleanup agent has the broader inventory.

Verification here was read-only source, diff and instruction inspection. I ran no builds, tests, linters, renderers or hosted checks, and changed no files or Git/GitHub state. Before completion, the integrated docs need strict build, generated-content and executable-example checks, plus real visual inspection of Material pages, navigation/search, version selection, mobile layout and rustdoc links.
